label: December 14–20
title: “I Have Loved You, Saith the Lord” —  Malachi

items.text: “I have loved you,” the Lord told His people through the prophet Malachi. Yet, after generations of affliction, they wondered, “Wherein hast thou loved us?” Despite their human weakness and rebellion, God never stopped reaching out in love, demonstrating His patient, enduring love through all of Israel’s history and continuing today.

When the sons of Jacob mistreated their brother Joseph, the Lord still saved them from famine. When Israel murmured in the wilderness, He fed them with manna. Even when Israel turned to other gods and were scattered, God promised that if they repented, He would gather and redeem them “with great mercies.”

Jesus Christ, “the Sun of Righteousness,” as Malachi called Him, has come “with healing in his wings.” He is the greatest evidence of God’s love for ancient Israel and for all of us today. His atoning sacrifice is the ultimate expression of divine love, offering hope and redemption.

As you study Malachi, look for questions the Lord asked the Israelites or they asked Him. Consider asking yourself similar questions to help you evaluate your relationship with the Lord and draw closer to Him. Are you feeling the Lord’s love? Are your offerings truly honoring Him?

In Malachi’s day, the Israelites needed to rebuild their relationship with the Lord. The Lord asked, “In what ways do I need to 'return' to the Lord?” and warned against robbing God. Evaluating our attitude during difficult times can reflect our feelings toward the Lord.

The Lord asks for “a pure offering.” What do your sacrifices to the Lord suggest about your feelings toward Him? Ponder what might make your offerings “polluted” or truly “pure.” True offerings are made with pure hearts and sincere devotion, not out of obligation or carelessness.

The Lord promises, “Return unto me, and I will return unto you.” When we show our faith by paying tithing, the Lord opens the windows of heaven. This invitation is a powerful reminder that obedience brings divine blessings and strengthens our faith in Him.

Paying tithing is an act of faith that invites blessings from the Lord. It strengthens our testimonies of Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ. The phrase “windows of heaven” beautifully describes how the Lord blesses us when we are obedient to His commandments.

Moroni quoted Malachi’s prophecy, “I will send you Elijah the prophet.” This prophecy is being fulfilled today as Elijah has come to restore the priesthood keys necessary for sealing families. This work turns the hearts of the fathers to the children and the children to the fathers.

Turning our hearts to our ancestors is profoundly important to Heavenly Father’s plan. The promises made to the fathers are being fulfilled through the sealing power restored by Elijah. This divine work connects generations and brings eternal blessings to all of God’s children.
